title: Report a partial VCF Installer configuration change
prompt:
Implement `VcfInstallerChange.psm1` as a PowerShell module for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused derivation of the pinned official VCF Installer OpenAPI specification; use its operationIds and wire contract, not a documentation page.

Export exactly these functions:

* `Connect-VcfInstallerChangeServer -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> [-Port <int>] [-Protocol <http|https>]` imports `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` version 13.5.0.25380678 or newer and calls `Connect-VcfInstallerServer` with a non-default connection.
* `Invoke-VcfInstallerChange -Connection <object> -MaxAllowedDomainsInSubscription <int> -ProxyHost <string> -ProxyPort <int> [-ProxyProtocol <HTTP|HTTPS>] [-CeipStatus <ENABLE|DISABLE>] [-PollIntervalSeconds <int>] [-TaskTimeoutSeconds <int>]` performs the three logical changes below in order.

The workflow must use the generated VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer initializers and invocation cmdlets for `updateSystemConfiguration`, `updateProxyConfiguration`, `getTask`, and `setCeipStatus` exactly as named in the contract. Connection setup remains the responsibility of `Connect-VcfInstallerServer`. First update the maximum allowed domains. Next enable and update the proxy, wait for the returned task to reach `SUCCESSFUL`, and retain its task id and terminal status. Finally update CEIP. Stop after the first failed logical step; do not roll back or misreport an earlier successful step. Do not use raw HTTP clients or vendor VMware modules.

Return one object with `Outcome` and `Steps`. `Outcome` is `Succeeded` when all three changes succeed, `Failed` when the first change fails, and `PartialFailure` when a later change fails after at least one success. `Steps` must always contain exactly three ordered records named `SystemConfiguration`, `ProxyConfiguration`, and `Ceip`, each with the ordered properties `Name`, `OperationId`, `Status`, `TaskId`, `TaskStatus`, `ErrorCode`, and `ErrorMessage`. Use `Succeeded`, `Failed`, or `NotRun` for step status. A failed VCF API call must preserve the API error code and message. A task that reaches a terminal failure state or times out counts as the proxy step failing. For a terminal task failure, preserve the first task error code and message when present; for a timeout, use error code `TASK_TIMEOUT` and message `Proxy task <task-id> did not finish within <timeout> seconds.`

Keep request objects minimal. In particular, the proxy request enables the proxy and sends only `isEnabled`, `host`, `port`, and `transferProtocol`; do not populate authentication fields or read-only fields. The protected verifier runs a contract-pinned loopback server and reads its request log. In addition to the generated operations, SDK 13.5 performs its own authenticated `GET /v1/sddc-manager` version probe while connecting; that SDK plumbing is expected and is not an extra workflow operation. The verifier checks full success, first-step failure, proxy API failure, proxy task failure and timeout, and a final CEIP HTTP 409 after two successes. It checks exact paths, methods, JSON member sets, values, order, authentication, stop behavior, task polling, omission of unset optional fields, and every report. It does not contact a live VMware endpoint.
scenario: A VCF Installer system limit update succeeds, its proxy update task completes successfully, and the later CEIP update is rejected with a conflict. The implementation must preserve the two earlier successes in its returned report.
constraints: Use VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer generated cmdlets; do not use raw HTTP clients.
Do not vendor VMware PowerCLI modules or contact a live VMware endpoint.
Omit unset optional and read-only fields from request JSON.
Stop after the first failed logical step and accurately report all three steps.
